text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of your eyes and skin; has this jaundice appeared within the first 24 hours of life, and is your baby feeding well?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic). The patient is a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed newborn with weight gain (3066g to 3200g), indicating adequate intake. The jaundice appearing after the first 24 hours and peaking around day 10-14 in exclusively breastfed infants is a classic presentation of breastfeeding jaundice, often due to suboptimal intake in the first few days leading to dehydration and increased enterohepatic circulation, rather than an underlying pathology. No further tests are needed; management involves ensuring frequent effective breastfeeding and hydration.
